analysis.title: Federal Reserve Monitor: October FOMC Preview: Expect the Policy Rate Will Move Higher, Just Not This Month
key_insights: MS expects the Fed to hold the target range at 3.75-4.0% in October with two hawkish dissents (Logan and Hammack). Chair Warsh is expected to signal further tightening while stressing a gradual, trend-dependent approach.

MS forecasts 25bp hikes in December and March for a terminal range of 4.25-4.5%. Risks are skewed toward more tightening, either quarterly hikes extending into 2027 or consecutive-meeting hikes starting in December.

No dissents would be a dovish surprise. Three or more dissents, explicit tightening guidance, or stronger inflation and energy-spillover language would be hawkish. MS views explicit forward guidance as unlikely given Warsh's stated preference for limiting it.

The September CPI upside surprise raises the risk of more persistent inflation. Second-round effects from higher energy prices could show in airline fares (+23% y/y), apparel, new and used vehicles, and motor vehicle equipment and supplies, offsetting the expected payback from the end of tariff pass-through.

MS sees few signs of overheating in the US economy. Employment growth is subdued, wage growth is decelerating and productivity is solid, while real consumer spending is growing at a reasonably solid pace. The import content of hyperscaler capex is expected to fuel price pressure abroad, particularly in Asia, more than at home.

MS argues against hiking at consecutive meetings. Markets assign only an 8-10% probability to an October hike, so a surprise could raise yields and tighten financial conditions by more than the 25bp move itself, with equities already reassessing the AI investment boom.
MS expects a statement that keeps the 'timelier return' inflation language and takes an information-based rather than forward-guidance approach. The October meeting has no updated projections.

MS rates strategists see scope for a hawkish October surprise because investors are still using the framework from before the June leadership change. A hawkish outcome could push Treasury yields lower and flatten the curve as growth concerns intensify.

The spread between market-implied trough and peak fed funds rates is -24bp versus a historical average of -131bp. MS thinks markets price too little easing between peak and trough. Since July 31 the implied peak is up 37bp and the implied trough is up 28bp.

The regression residual of the 10-year Treasury yield versus the implied trough rate has fallen to about -2bp. MS reads this as stronger demand for duration and lower required compensation for holding Treasuries. Treasuries are regaining their risk-off hedging properties versus the S&P 500.

MS FX strategists expect the USD to stay supported after an October hold. Reasons are US-rest-of-world rate differentials, USD longs as a hedge against rising global yields (JPY is the most exposed G10 currency), and European risks including wider sovereign spreads and uncertainty before the April 2027 French presidential election. MS puts USD/JPY fair value above 170.

MS agency MBS strategists are long the basis. Spreads are near 12-month wides and technicals support next year, including deregulatory capital rules, deposit growth above loan growth, a possible $75bn of Norges Bank additions and room for GSE buying. Near-term demand is unlikely to return in size until volatility falls and the Fed path is clearer.

About $58bn of existing floating-rate agency MBS could be capped out if the Fed hikes three times in line with market pricing, and the amount could double with more aggressive hikes. Floaters underperformed their collateral in September.

MS muni strategists note the S&P municipal index yield has rallied more than 40bp in October, saving issuers 3% or more versus pricing at the peak. They expect the forward calendar to recover as issuers focus on future Fed hikes, with ratings report filings possibly returning to the 2025 run rate.

risk_factors: A Fed hike larger or faster than markets price, or an unexpected October hike, could lift yields and tighten financial conditions by more than the move itself.
Energy price pass-through into core goods could make inflation stickier.
AI-related equity volatility and wider corporate bond spreads could tighten financial conditions further.
Demand-side price pressure from the AI spending boom could emerge with a lag.
Floating-rate agency MBS face capping risk if the Fed hikes more than expected.
European political and fiscal risk, including the French presidential election in April 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: inflation remains above target, the economy is resilient, and supply shocks plus solid demand risk entrenching inflation, so a hike in October would reinforce price stability and reduce the chance of more aggressive tightening later.
tension_points.bear_case: MS base case: a hold with a gradual path is better. Markets price only an 8-10% chance of an October hike, so a surprise could lift yields and tighten financial conditions by more than 25bp while equities already reassess the AI boom.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Three or more hawkish dissents, explicit tightening guidance, or stronger inflation and energy-spillover language at the October FOMC would favor the faster-hike view.

tension_points.theme: Treasury duration after a hawkish Fed
tension_points.bull_case: A hawkish October outcome lowers the implied trough rate, pulls Treasury yields down and flattens the curve as growth concerns outweigh inflation, with Treasuries regaining hedge value.
tension_points.bear_case: Further inflation surprises could push yields higher as markets price a faster pace of tightening or a higher terminal rate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further rise in the market-implied peak rate with no decline in the implied trough rate would undercut the flattening call.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed is expected to hold in October and prefer a gradual path of 25bp hikes in December and March over hikes at consecutive meetings.
theme_stances.evidence: A measured recalibration remains our base case

theme_stances.key_argument: A hawkish October FOMC would push Treasury yields lower and flatten the curve as growth risks rise.
theme_stances.evidence: Treasuries do not need the Fed to begin cutting rates to provide effective protection.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rate differentials and exposure of JPY to rising global yields favor USD/JPY longs.
theme_stances.evidence: JPY is the G10 currency most negatively exposed to increases in average global yields
